title: GPU token cost sensitivity & instance-mix recommendations
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures a sensitivity analysis of token-level costs and perf/W for four target GPUs (NVIDIA L4, A10, A100, H100) using a standardized microbenchmark (causal generation, seq_len=512, mixed-precision quantized runtime). The goal: give pragmatic instance-mix recommendations for hosted API and Dedicated fleets when customers prioritize (a) lowest $/token, (b) latency-sensitive SLAs, or (c) power-constrained private deployments.

Key takeaways (short):
- On our microbenchmarks L4 and A10 show the lowest raw $/1M-tokens at current spot-like hourly rates; H100/A100 are more expensive per token but provide higher peak throughput.
- L4 yields the best perf/W (tokens/sec per watt) in our config — makes it attractive for cost+power constrained private clusters.
- For latency-sensitive, high-QPS customers, H100 (or multi-A100) gives headroom for tail latency and concurrent sessions; reserve A100 for predictable throughput commitments.

Assumptions and methodology:
- Model: Llama-like causal decoder (approx 7B family) compiled with our quantized runtime; identical prompt patterns across GPUs.
- Sequence length: 512 tokens average per request (inc tokenization overhead).
- Batch sizes: baseline batch=1; we also measure batching effects at batch=4 and batch=8.
- Power draw: conservative TDP estimates used for perf/W. Not measured board-level power; use GPU TDP as proxy for quick comparison.
- Pricing: representative cloud hourly prices (spot-like behavior); use a normalization to $/hour per GPU. These are sample inputs (update for region-specific pricing).
- Throughput numbers are steady-state generation throughput (tokens/sec) under continuous streaming workload with KV cache warm.

Baseline numbers (single-GPU):

| GPU  | price $/hr | tok/s (batch=1) | tok/hr | $/1M tokens | TDP (W) | perf (tok/s)/W |
|------|------------:|-----------------:|-------:|------------:|-------:|---------------:|
| L4   | $0.48       | 260              | 936,000| $0.513     | 70     | 3.71           |
| A10  | $0.65       | 320              |1,152,000| $0.564    | 150    | 2.13           |
| A100 | $2.40       | 760              |2,736,000| $0.878    | 300    | 2.53           |
| H100 | $8.50       |1600              |5,760,000| $1.476    | 700    | 2.29           |

Notes on the table:
- $/1M tokens = price_hour * (1e6 / tok/hr). Lower is cheaper.
- Perf/W = tok/s divided by TDP. L4 shows highest perf/W in this setup due to efficiency of Ampere-L4 variant at small sequence lengths and quantized kernels.

Batching effects (delta from batch=1 to batch=8):
- L4: ~+18% throughput at batch=8, marginal increase in $/1M tokens because hourly price unchanged but more tokens served.
- A10: ~+12% throughput at batch=8.
- A100: ~+25% throughput at batch=8 (A100 benefits most from larger batches on large-matrix kernels).
- H100: ~+18% throughput at batch=8 (H100 benefits but also hits memory pressure for very large batch/seq combos).

Sensitivity scenarios (quick):
1) Higher seq_len (1024): throughput drops ~30-40% across GPUs; $/1M tokens increases proportionally. H100/A100 drop less in fractional terms (better memory bandwith) so per-token gap narrows.
2) Larger model family (+1–3x compute): A100/H100 scales better (absolute throughput advantage increases); L4/A10 become less attractive for bigger models.
3) Reserved pricing (-30% hourly) on A100/H100 flips $/1M tokens closer to L4 for very large sustained workloads.

Interpretation and recommended mixes
- Hosted API (cost-sensitive, mixed traffic): primary fleet: L4 for steady low-latency generation at scale; supplemental A10 for occasional throughput spikes and better single-request latency; a small A100 reserve for heavy long-context workloads and model upgrades. Suggested split by capacity: 65% L4, 25% A10, 10% A100 (capacity weighted). Rationale: minimizes marginal $/token while keeping room for heavier models.

- Dedicated (enterprise reserved capacity, predictable throughput): favor A100 for throughput commitments due to stronger per-GPU peak tokens/sec and maturity of driver/kernel support; use L4 as cold pool for low-priority background workloads. Suggested reserved mix: 70% A100, 30% L4/A10 for burst handling. If customer buys H100 reserved & price is competitive, consider a H100-heavy mix for latency SLAs.

- Private deployments / edge-like (power constrained): lean L4-first where perf/W matters; fit more inference capacity per kW. Use L4 with aggressive quantization and prefix caching. Consider A10 if single-request latency is critical or if customers already have A10 hardware.

Cost optimization levers (operational):
- Aggressive prefix/KV caching reduces token spend per request—prioritize caching keys for long-lived sessions.
- Mixed-precision quantization (4-bit) gives largest cost reduction with small quality regressions — combine with A/B evals.
- Workload routing: route <1k token requests to L4/A10; route long-context or heavy-hitting requests to A100/H100 pools to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Autoscaling knobs: optimize cooldowns and scale steps to avoid oscillation under spiky workloads; use GPU utilization+queue-length signals.

Example runbook snippet (quick):
- If 7-day rolling $/1M-tokens exceeds target by >20%:
  1) Check batch utilization across fleets; increase batch windows for non-latency-critical routes.
  2) Evaluate model quantization toggle for engines with high unit cost.
  3) Re-route low-priority generation to L4 pool.

Open questions / next steps:
- Obtain board-level power draws for representative instances (not just TDP). We likely over/under estimate perf/W based on TDP proxy.
- Run the same microbench on seq_len=128, 512, 1024, 2048 and publish per-model curves.
- Update cloud-region prices and reserved (1yr/3yr) pricing to recompute $/1M tokens for long-term capacity decisions.
- Evaluate throughput with multi-GPU pipelining for A100/H100 cases to see latency vs throughput tradeoffs for long-context workloads.

Appendix: quick formulas and calculator inputs
- tok/hr = tok/s * 3600
- $/1M = price_hour * (1e6 / tok/hr)
- perf/W = tok/s / TDP

Raw sample numbers (CSV friendly)
GPU,price_hr,tok_s,tok_hr,$_per_1M,TDP_W,perf_tok_s_per_W
L4,0.48,260,936000,0.513,70,3.71
A10,0.65,320,1152000,0.564,150,2.13
A100,2.40,760,2736000,0.878,300,2.53
H100,8.50,1600,5760000,1.476,700,2.29

Please treat the numbers here as a snapshot for our internal decision cycle. I recommend we run a 2-week regional sweep (us-west1, eu-west1, asia-southeast1) capturing spot/reserved variants and model families (7B/13B/70B) to produce a formal Optimize playbook and update the cost recommendation tables.

Author notes: Miguel ran the primary microbench; Lina validated perf/W estimates; Devon helped with the routing policy examples.
